newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer denies Germany has softened EMU stance.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer denies Germany has softened EMU stance.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Monday denied newspaper reports alleging Germany had softened its position on the entry criteria for Europe's currency union.

Several British newspapers this morning reported that Germany had distanced itself from its hardline demands that nations' budget deficits must be at three percent in order to qualify for currency union.
"When I was in Noordwijk, and I was there, I had not heard of any change," Tietmeyer said in response to a question whether there had been any softening of Germany's stance on EMU criteria.

Germany has been one of Europe's strongest supporters of a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty, arguing the future European currency, the euro, can only be strong if members' economies have reached sufficient conversion.

Asked whether EMU was still scheduled to begin on time in 1999, Tietmeyer said the group of 10 central bank governors committee had not discussed EMU at its meeting today. But Tietmeyer said "I can confirm that this date is in the Treaty."
Tietmeyer however said he could not comment on speculation about Germany having backed off its EMU stance.
